summary: Biola University — a private institution with roughly 4,000 students — sits right in the middle of La Mirada, giving this otherwise quiet 7.8-square-mile suburban pocket an unexpected anchor that most people outside southeast Los Angeles County don't realize exists. The campus adds a small but real employment base to a city that otherwise functions as a bedroom community; the I-5 freeway slices along its eastern edge, funneling commuters toward downtown LA (about 20 miles northwest) or south toward Anaheim and Irvine, and the typical rush-hour grind runs 45 minutes to well over an hour depending on direction. With a median home price around $763,200 against a median household income of $110,177, the price-to-income ratio lands near 6.9 — stretched but not quite as punishing as coastal Orange County, and the 6.5% poverty rate signals a relatively stable economic floor. The terrain is gently rolling, part of the low hills between the San Gabriel River corridor and the Puente Hills to the north, which means some rooftops catch decent sunset views westward. La Mirada Regional Park, a genuine 50-plus-acre green space with a swimming complex, fishing lake, and splash pad, provides a surprisingly substantial outdoor amenity for a city this compact. Climate-wise, 9.4 hours of daily sunshine and average highs around 76°F mean year-round outdoor usability, though summer inland heat pushes noticeably above that average. La Mirada delivers the stability and spacing of mid-density suburbia — the tradeoff is that almost everything beyond errands and evening walks requires a car and a freeway on-ramp.
